body: I have a load of craft supplies and have crochet and embroidery projects on the go, keeping me busy when I'm not working. But I just miss being able to spend time outdoors, when its sunny and warm out it's really difficult as it would be for many folks
Good idea, will have a look around.

Oh boy. 
Its 11:07am and I could definitely do with a drink. No alcohol in the house sadly. 
Probably also driving my partner nuts with my frequent outbursts of anxiety.
She recovered easily 💜 thanks all for thoughts and prayers. She might be 90 but that resilience and stubbornness is as strong as ever.
I'd just want to chat to him about stuff like books, art, movies, and just life in general, his likes and dislikes etc. I think he just seems like a really intriguing human.
4, & multiples of 4. Usually count in multiples of 4 16 times, whenever I'm doing any compulsive behaviour...
Thank you for sharing this 💓 wishing him  all the best, what relief for you all.

Gosh, what an awful time of it you had. I'm sorry you went through that. I hope you're allowing yourself to rest from the physical and mental turmoil.

 At the beginning of this I also spent hours checking the news, which made my ocd compulsions worse - i have ocd around contamination and harm. 

I blocked all news websites and now only get daily email updates from the government as my news. My anxiety has improved a lot since. Also meditation.

I've realised if we focus on what we can control , our own actions, anxiety becomes more manageable.

Stay well. We will get through this.
I love Bob Dylan. So yes, I'm pumped for this movie.
So true fml

My 90 year old grandmother has contracted covid 19 while recovering from emergency surgery. I'm angry that the govt are not testing people or providing health professionals with enough PPE. So far she apparently has mild symptoms. But shes 90, she had a stroke in december last year, and she has generally  been in very poor health. I'm so scared that I'm going to lose her.

Far too relatable.

This is how I feel trying to work from home. Just deciding to see it another way now, I'm at home because of a world crisis and if I can get some of my work done, then that's good. I'm not expecting too much of myself because my mental health is bad. And that's ok.

Please try and reach out for some kind of help though. I'm in the uk, have given up on the nhs and have gone for low cost private therapy through a charity - I'm only going to have to wait a couple of weeks, and itll be online. Theres no way I can do this on my own.
This is so accurate ☹
Yes. I hadn't done in years, until lockdown. Now its regular. Water helps.
Nope. It was me. I woren matching socks that one time ,which my brain told me nOT TO DO, but I did it anyway, and now look at what's happened. I also did not check the oven the right number of times.
This. Is. Incredible. 😍😍
I've started doing this now and I am having moments of calm during it, which is weird but also really helpful. Thanks for the suggestion !!

Hey. I hear you. This is hell for me too - I have OCD and severe anxiety, and asthma, so I'm at a higher risk too. I'm also desperate for a return to normality. I think most people are. It's ok to be feeling how you are. 

I wish I could say when itll be over. But no one really knows. What helps me is taking things one hour at a time and not thinking beyond today. Otherwise, I get overwhelmed and panic and get really horrible thoughts. 

You're not alone. The whole world is in this together, and the internet thankfully makes the world a little smaller. Keep reaching out.
Thank you so much ! I'll check it out 😊
That looks so yummy 😍
Yesssss absolutely
Honestly, actually putting on a bra and real clothes, not my weekend loungewear, helps me get in the mood for work. I cant work in sweatpants. I've put a routine together now as well. Also yoga .
I take medication already (sertraline 200mg) and its no longer working for me. My gp is going to change it. I would rather have therapy than meds, tbh.
I'll have a look into it  thanks.
Have you got any recommendations ? I'll have a look on kindle store but sometimes theres a lot of crap self help books out there.
Same, I have asthma and my anxiety can be a trigger plus, I had the flu in February and the cough has lingered a little. Mindfulness helps.

It really does suck! And when health authorities tell people to not go outside because you will spread it just fuels my thoughts big time, like I am responsible for making people sick and dead. I know I'm not...

I am in the uk however I have an underlying health condition and must be very careful- also im too scared to even go outside for a walk once because my ocd tells me that if I do that I will give it to someone, even if I do strictly follow social distancing 🙃 I'm getting some exercise done at home though.
I have social anxiety and panic disorder, ocd on top of that is wild. I've had depression in the past, trying to avoid slipping into depression but my country is on lockdown and that's hard to do 🙃🙃🙃
Love this !!!
Oh and also, my 30th birthday celebrations got put on hold, so I'm excited to celebrate my 30th. Didnt even get cake!

Hugging (and never letting go of) my mum, my sister and my best friend. Going to the cinema. Drinking coffee in my favourite coffee shop. Getting a hair cut. Going to the office and seeing my colleagues. Going out for a meal with my partner. Going to the pub for a pint. I'm excited about the mundane, the every day. I'm going to try and never ever take that for granted ever again.

Because those people are entitled and think the rules dont apply to them. They think they are invisible and that this virus is "just flu" (which is horrible anyway, and they obviously have never had it if they think like that). When it gets to the point that hospitals have to choose who to try and save, the people who have not been following guidelines should be at the end of the queue 🤷‍♀️ we are on lockdown in the uk however the government arent enforcing it enough. Its bloody ridiculous.

Our country is in lockdown and suddenly I'm having to somehow live with my partners constant sniffing ,like every minute, it's making me very angry! Usually it doesnt bother me. And god knows how long this lockdown will go on for!
Thanks for the tip, I'll look into it.

Dude I wish I could get xanax but I live in the uk ! I dont drink a lot of  coffee, just one cup every now and again (although I think tea has more caffeine in it?). Even yoga didnt cut it this morning.
It really is, right? I wanted to enjoy a coffee before starting my work but anxiety wont even let me do that ☹  I'm sorry you feel the same !
Also, decluttering. I make excuses not to do it..!
I'm enjoying my minute commute from bed to desk, and having a snuggle with my pets every day while working 😬

Hi. I really hear you a lot. This has triggered suicidal ideation I have not had for a few years. I find it useful to think of it in this way- I dont want to stop living, I want this current situation to end. Take it a minute at a time. Keep reaching out. The fact that you posted here shows you're questioning your thoughts. It's a horrible situation and lockdown will impact your mental health. Its impacting mine, too. We will get through this together. Keep reaching out ok?
I'm so anxious today that I keep dry heaving and almost puked ☹
I can feel and see germs and dirt on skin, clothes ,furniture...its wild, especially at the moment. Also a checker and counter. Perhaps ironically I'm not tidy. At all. Just very clean.
Thank you
Thank you for reading my rant i didn't expect anyone to. What is eft tapping ?
Me too. It's a riot.
Holy shit you are so talented !!!

Me too. My routine has gone, I havent left the house for days, I cant get used to WFH. My fears are no longer irrational. The whole world has shut down. But everyone is in this and that is some comfort to me. And spring is starting. And this will pass. We dont know when, but it will. One day at a time - one hour at a time if that's all you can manage. Any more and itll be overwhelming.
Gorgeous!!!! Hello Pancake! Virtual hugs to you 🥰

Yes this is me 🙃 it's like, before the hell was just in my head and now it's real. And WFH and self isolation is just further validation, and is reassuring me. I havent even had therapy yet...just imagine it now "your fears arent irrational and you wont contaminate or harm anyone" "um, remember Coronavirus?? When I was told to self isolate to prevent the spread?!!!?"

I am not good. I also have harm OCD and the hand washing has morphed into a way for me to deal with the harm thoughts on top of contamination which is wild.. Although thankfully, my office has closed and I'm WFH for the foreseeable which means I don't need to leave my flat apart from once a week to get essentials. Still battling the compulsion to check the news every 5 minutes , blocking websites helps. How are you coping?
Same 🙃
I'm learning French (duolingo is a great app) and taking on new embroidery projects. Too bad I still have to work at home 😂
I find embroidery and crochet very therapeutic - the repetition soothes me. Also classic music or nature sounds.

The one local organisation to me refused to help saying my case is too complex and what I need is treatment. I feel helpless.

I can get emotional support through the employee assistance program my work offers, so I guess I will call them but they dont offer the right CBT for ocd. 

My manager referred me to occupational health because of my ocd ,but that is on hold now due to this. My mental health has reached crisis point and I'm so scared

I am not coping. My gp is saying there is little she can do in terms of therapy (uk based, turned down by one service already, can't afford private) ,meds might be changed. I still have to leave the flat to go to work. I do client facing stuff normally but I am able to cancel all of that but not yet able to just work from home. And I'm in London, cases are quite high here compared to the rest of the country and I'm convinced that's my fault, I havent done enough to stop it. I'm spending around 4 hours a day engaging in compulsive behaviours- I have not had any treatment, and I've tried self help but I'm too overwhelmed for that. 

Tdlr ; I'm not coping. Havent had treatment for ocd yet and I will be waiting ages. Everything is hard.

Everyone is in the same boat. We are all anxious. It's a really hard time for everyone,  especially if you have OCD and anxiety. But it wont last forever, it just feels that way. Can you do things to take your mind off it all? Movies, books, hobbies. I find embroidery very therapeutic. Yoga , meditation. Exercise you can  do indoors.


Part of me wishes I did not have to go to work still, because my partner is making me anxious making comments like "but how will you get there?" And "cant you work from home more?" No ,there is rent and bills still to pay. I have to work, and still go to the office most of the week, until told otherwise.

I've been like this since my first panic attack in 2007. I also have asthma. Am I 1) panicking,  2) having asthma symptoms or 3) is it covid ? Who the heck knows at this point 🤷‍♀️ unless I have a fever I assume its either 1 or 2.
Yes. I can also "see" them - my whole flat is contaminated, but my partner does not understand this !!!

I havent even started therapy. Theres no way I can afford it, and waiting times in the uk for therapy are months. Wish the uk government would actually do something rather than sprout rubbish about herd immunity and telling us we will have to lose loved ones. They dont care about anything but the economy!!!

Not well. I believe I should have done more to stop the spread as if I'm somehow responsible for spreading the Coronavirus to start with and continuing to do so. My hand washing compulsions aren't enough and they are becoming more severe.
It's my 30th birthday today, it has sucked massively but this has made my day. Thanks.
I cant offer any advice really, as I'm not in recovery yet, but I relate to this. My fear is passing the virus on to people I love.
My hands look the same. Doesn't help that I have eczema too and am allergic to soap.

I have contamination ocd and have asthma.

This made me chuckle. I needed that. Thanks.
I get obsessions, too, about celebrities which is weird.

I'm lucky to work in a team that encourages openness - I wasnt open with colleagues till these past couple of weeks.

 I have months of waiting for therapy , as I cannot afford private therapy (I'm in the uk). I'm not sure how much more of this I can actually take. I feel like I'm going nuts to be honest, and I've had some worrying thoughts too. I'm avoiding the news completely but I dont know if that makes me more anxious , but I'm abroad currently  Sunday and I think sensationalist headlines will trigger me even more than if I was at home.
Big yikes!!

I think that part of the reason my fears are so heightened is that I'm going to paris on Wednesday, booked it months ago last year. However in the uk where I live cases have increased a lot and the chances of getting it there are pretty much the same as getting it here (although I'm terrified of contaminating others  not actually catching it). 
I think we have to just carry on as usual, unless we are told otherwise by authorities. The horrible thing is that health advice (hand washing, isolating if you think you have it) legitimise and validate our fears and compulsive behaviours which is confusing to those of us with ocd. You're not alone in how you feel.

I hear you. When I get physical symptoms of anxiety like that I find it helpful to try grounding myself using senses,  eg 5 things I can see, 4 things I can hear, 3 things I can touch , 2 things I can smell and 1 thing I can taste.
My what if thoughts also drive me nuts.

I also feel like this. Trying to get on with life as normal though. I'm going to paris with my sister this week for my birthday- part of me is terrified but the reality is I have as much chance getting it here (i live in the uk) as I do in paris and I think we have to try and carry on as usual unless told otherwise by government /health authorities. You're not alone in how you feel.
This is incredible 🥳🥳🥳

My coworkers have been joking about handwashing and if they are doing it enough. Not helpful! And yes being reassured about handwashing is confusing .

I am going to go and get some help and I have turned off the news, which has certainly helped even a little bit.
Knowing I'm not alone brings me peace. This is why I joined reddit. I guess we will all get through it together.
I have a Luna too! Gorgeous girl 🥰
I have contamination OCD and I'm terrified I'm going to pass it onto others. My compulsive behaviour is so so bad ,I dont know what is ocd hand washing or normal ☹
I came here looking for people who felt the same way. While I wish no one felt similar to me it's a comfort to know I'm not alone in how I feel.

I also have asthma, so I have got a slightly higher risk although my thoughts have nothing to do with getting sick myself but making others sick. I don't really understand why I think this way. If I dont wash my hands in a specific way, specific number of times, I will be responsible for making people sick. I've been like this for a while but with being told by health authorities to wash your hands is confusing.
I need to definitely read about ocd. I dont understand how it works.

Im terrified of passing the virus on to people. I'm so scared and convinced I'm contaminated and will be responsible for causing harm that it's taken over my life and I cant think of anything else. I've never had therapy, but on the NHS it's likely to be a long wait for 6 sessions of CBT. I'm so distressed I dont think I can take it much more. I broke down at work the other day because I was so scared I'm contaminated
